name: Maelstrom
desc: A great whirlpool turning under a bruised sky — the sea bending away into a funnel whose throat swallows the light, foam dragged into a tightening spiral because the water near the centre turns so much faster than the water at the rim, spray hazing the far reach toward a lit horizon; as a storm-lit maelstrom, sumi ink vortex, a surveyor's contour chart of the surface itself, false-color thermal, or spectral.

energy.doc: circulation — funnel depth, spin rate and how hard the foam is dragged into the spiral (the master knob)

scale.doc: size of the vortex — from a tight deep drain to a slow ocean-wide gyre

speed.doc: rotation and evolution rate (0.2 still turns)

density.doc: foam detail — the count of streaks dragged around the gyre, from a few broad ribbons to a fine shredded lace

haze.doc: spray and distance haze — from hard clear air to a drowned white murk swallowing the far reach

hue.doc: hue of the sea (the sky takes the complement)

x.doc: where the throat sits across the sea

y.doc: horizon height — camera pitch, from a low sea-level view to looking down into the gyre

style.doc: aesthetic: storm-lit sea with a swallowing throat / sumi ink vortex on paper / abstracted surveyor's contour chart of the solved free surface / false-color thermal / spectral

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the foam field and cloud decks
